nodes.html: Selected Members: Chia Yun Wu, Katherine Sidelsky, Lieh Sugai

As a medium, photography is composed of a myriad of chemistries that can be beautifully realized physically, digitally, abstractly, psychically.  By “beautifully”, I mean to emphasize the mysterious connection between an affectionate process and how that sentiment moves through the life of the resulting image. How we, as viewers, encounter this life is not a prescriptive or predictable experience. 

Lieh Sugai, Chia Yun Wu and Katherine Sidelsky are affectionately using the photographic substrate’s ability to absorb chaos and to carry on sculpting environments where they can contend with the complex reality of displacement, longing and connection. 

I am drawn to artists who wield the flexibility of photography to render nearly impossible things. Each of these three artists skillfully grapples with very distinct life experiences. Their respective practices and bodies of work are inspiring examples of how photography can traverse dimensions of times, states, and histories.

-Hernease Davis

About the Juror:


Hernease Davis is a photo-based artist and curator, whose practice is spurred by her curiosity about process, one’s psychological nature and the meaningful connections made possible through art when individual complexities are acknowledged and welcomed. Hernease uses photography, crochet and sound to create multi-sensorial installations that explore complex notions of empathy. Hernease’s work has been exhibited throughout the U.S., including the International Center of Photography, Silver Eye Center for Photography, Transformer Station/Cleveland Museum of Art and the Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts. Hernease is an Assistant Curator at the Visual Studies Workshop (VSW), and the producer of The Project Space podcast, which features artists who have participated in VSW’s long-running residency program.
